summary: A city caps yearly rent increases, building slows, and the council later lets rents reset between tenants and exempts newer buildings.
realLife: St. Paul voters capped rent increases at 3 percent in 2021. In September 2022 the council let owners raise rent by more than the cap, up to 8 percent plus inflation, once a tenant leaves; later the council permanently exempted newer buildings, citing fewer permits and a need to show the city welcomed development.
sources: CBS Minnesota, St. Paul council approves rent control change, Sep 2022: https://www.cbsnews.com/minnesota/news/st-paul-city-council-approves-rent-control-change
KSTP, St. Paul City Council votes to roll back rent stabilization ordinance: https://kstp.com/kstp-news/local-news/st-paul-city-council-votes-to-roll-back-rent-stabilization-ordinance/

turns.way: The council exempts only buildings under a set age and leaves the rest capped.
